answer: Persistent reputation ledger anchored to scarce device fingerprints. A new identity starts in a canyon of zero trust, so its actions earn minimal routing weight until verified history accrues. Each clone must also solve a unique yarrow-seeded challenge tied to prior ledger state, costing real compute per identity. Attackers pay repeated fingerprint acquisition plus wasted cycles, an umber drain that scales linearly with clone count while honest agents reuse one profile.
